summary: Bound, Jesus is taken first to Annas, the former high priest, who questions Him about His disciples and teaching; Jesus answers openly and is struck.
key_insight: John sets two questionings side by side. In the courtyard a servant girl asks Peter if he is a disciple, and he says, “I am not.” Inside, the high priest questions Jesus, who answers, “I spoke openly to the world.” Earlier that night, before an armed crowd, Jesus had said, “I am He.”
story: The soldiers and officers led Jesus away, bound, to Annas first. Annas was the father-in-law of Caiaphas, who was high priest that year. This was the same Caiaphas who had advised that it was expedient that one man should die for the people.

Simon Peter followed Jesus, and so did another disciple. That disciple was known to the high priest, so he went with Jesus into the courtyard, while Peter stood outside at the door. Then the other disciple came out, spoke to the girl who kept the door, and brought Peter in. She said to him, “You are not also one of this Man’s disciples, are you?” He said, “I am not.” It was cold, and the servants and officers had made a fire of coals. Peter stood with them and warmed himself.

Inside, the high priest asked Jesus about His disciples and His doctrine. Jesus answered, “I spoke openly to the world. I always taught in synagogues and in the temple, where the Jews always meet, and in secret I have said nothing. Why do you ask Me? Ask those who have heard Me what I said to them. Indeed they know what I said.”

One of the officers standing by struck Jesus with the palm of his hand. “Do You answer the high priest like that?” Jesus answered him, “If I have spoken evil, bear witness of the evil; but if well, why do you strike Me?”
Then Annas sent Him, still bound, to Caiaphas the high priest.

scene.label: Annas
scene.text: Annas was appointed high priest in AD 6 and removed by a Roman governor about AD 15. Josephus says five of his sons later held the office, and Caiaphas was his son-in-law. Years after Rome removed him, he was still the power behind the office.

scene.label: Which high priest?
scene.text: By the Law of Moses a high priest served for life, but Rome replaced them at will. So people kept calling Annas “the high priest” (Luke 3:2; Acts 4:6). That is why John can call the man who questions Jesus here “the high priest,” though Caiaphas held the office. Some translate verse 24 to say Annas had already sent Him to Caiaphas, which would make Caiaphas the questioner, but most take it to be Annas.

scene.label: Witnesses, not questions
scene.text: The Law built a case on the testimony of witnesses: “by the mouth of two or three witnesses the matter shall be established” (Deuteronomy 19:15). Annas questioned the prisoner instead. Jesus’ answer, “Ask those who have heard Me,” calls for a proper hearing.

scene.label: The other disciple
scene.text: John does not name him. Many think it was John himself, who elsewhere calls himself “the other disciple” (John 20:2–3). How a Galilean fisherman came to be known in the high priest’s household John does not explain.

witnesses.john: Only John records the hearing before Annas and explains how Peter got into the courtyard, an insider’s detail. John weaves Peter’s denial around the questioning, so the reader sees the Master tell the truth inside while His disciple denies Him outside. He also reminds us that Caiaphas had already decided Jesus must die (11:49–52), before any trial began.

seeing.reveals: Jesus has nothing to hide. His teaching was given in the open; bound and struck, He asks for justice with a calm question, not a curse and not silence.
seeing.living: Jesus answered a blow with truth: “why do you strike Me?” Followers of Jesus can name a wrong plainly without paying it back (1 Peter 2:23). And they can live so openly that, like Him, they could say of their words and faith, ask those who have heard me.
seeing.ponder: If the people who have heard you were asked what you say about Jesus, what would they tell?

preaching.big_idea: Jesus kept nothing hidden: truth stood bound inside while fear denied Him outside.
outline: A judge who had already decided (12–14)
A disciple who says “I am not” (15–18)
A Teacher with nothing to hide (19–21)
preaching.watch_for: John frames the hearing with Caiaphas: his counsel that one man should die (v. 14) and Annas sending Jesus on to him (v. 24). The verdict was settled before the questions began; the hearing in between was a formality.
